videos.why: The owner's Nike remake: the Swoosh is on shoes everywhere, frame 0 is a Swoosh close-up, and now every picture is new (16 across 7 beats), with a depth shot of Knight, a punch montage, a timeline, Nike's results headline and an overlay on every beat. The ring, the shares and the $46.4B are held back. Ranked above rank's 4.6 because the taste penalty comes from the stale original this remake fixes.
strengths: A thing the viewer owns, known in every country
Every picture once, a big red Swoosh on the cover
Twist (ring + 500 shares) held to the turn, payoff on a new figure
risks: The 1971 drawing in the student beat is low-contrast (a kit issue with transparent PNGs)
The $35 Swoosh topic is crowded in search (study, 20 Nov)

videos.why: The owner-approved Stanley remake: a cup-in-your-hand story told over 16 different pictures, with a depth shot, montages, a sales chart, the CNBC headline and a gold $750M payoff. Its format scores low and Stanley is better known in the US than worldwide, so it goes second. Ranked above rank's 2.1 because the taste penalty comes from the stale original this remake fixes.
strengths: Product craze people recognise, a real limit sign on the cover
Sales climb shown bar by bar with the source
Payoff held back for the poster; the loop lands on the opening shelf
